t: Tara, Tambay Tayo. Ang Bagong Istambayan ng Bayan. ("Come on, let's hang out. The nation's new hangout spot.") Diskarte is an open-source, self-hostable community platform — text chat, voice, video and screen sharing — made for Filipino gamers, student organisations, creators and barkadas. It can run entirely on free tiers of Vercel (or Render), Supabase and LiveKit. Diskarte is Filipino for resourcefulness: finding a clever way to get things done with what you have. The product leans into that — low-data mode for prepaid connections, an offline outbox for patchy signal, an installable app instead of app-store downloads, and a deployment that costs ₱0.

Term Meaning Tambayan A community server (from tambay, to hang out). Routes live under /tambayan Diskarte HQ The system Tambayan every account joins automatically; hosts #announcements and #global-lounge Bantay-Bayan The moderation toolkit ("community watch"): auto-mod, bans, audit log Salakot The mascot's hat; the default avatars are recoloured salakot mascots LFG "Looking for group" beacons that drop party members straight into a voice channel Moments 24-hour text/photo updates shown to friends Control Center The super-admin panel at /admin Rank A member's built-in role in a Tambayan: Member, Moderator or Admin (plus the owner) Role A custom, coloured label admins create; can grant access to private channels

The database is the security boundary. Row Level Security, guard triggers and checked RPCs enforce every rule, so no client path can skip them. See architecture. Honest interfaces. Features that need an unapplied migration or missing configuration say so instead of failing silently; sample content on the landing page is labelled as such. Built for real connections. Optimistic sends with idempotent retries, an offline queue, reconnect recovery, low-data mode and a 30-second call rejoin. Accessible by default. Keyboard operation, visible focus, reduced motion and transparency, high contrast and axe audits in the test suite. No AI features. Diskarte has no generative or automated-moderation AI; reports are triaged by people.

Go to the Diskarte website and choose Sign up (or continue with Google/GitHub if you see those buttons). Enter your email, a username (3–32 lowercase letters, numbers, _ or . — people add you with it, like @juan.dc), a display name, and a password. Your password needs at least 10 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a symbol. The checklist under the box turns green as you go. Check your email and tap the confirmation link (if you don't see it, look in Spam). Set up your profile: pick a salakot avatar colour or upload a photo, add a banner and a short bio. You're now in Diskarte and already a member of Diskarte HQ. Home shows a short Getting started checklist — join or create a Tambayan, add a friend, say hello, install the app — that ticks itself off as you go. Hide it anytime with the ✕. Sample data. If sign-up says registrations are paused, the community running this Diskarte only accepts invited members for now. Forgot your password? On the sign-in page choose Forgot your password?, enter your email, and follow the link we send.

Diskarte is a web app you can install — no app store needed. Installing gives you a home-screen icon, a full-screen app and (on iPhone) notifications. iPhone or iPad (iOS 16.4 or newer) Open Diskarte in Safari. Tap the Share button (square with an arrow). Choose Add to Home Screen, then Add. Open Diskarte from your home screen. To get notifications, go to Settings → Notifications and turn them on for this device. Android (Chrome) Open Diskarte in Chrome. Tap the ⋮ menu → Install app (or Add to Home screen). Open it from your home screen or app drawer. Computer (Chrome or Edge) — click the install icon in the address bar, or Settings → Storage & Data → Install Diskarte. Updating: when a new version is ready, Settings → Storage & Data shows Reload to update. Finish any call first.

Open User settings (gear next to your name, bottom left; on phones, the Profile tab): My Profile — avatar, banner, display name, bio. Status — click your avatar in the bottom-left panel to set Online, Idle, Do Not Disturb or Invisible, or pick a fun status like Nagluto ng Canton or Nasa jeep, mahina signal. Choose Clear after 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours or 24 hours so you don't forget it. Appearance — themes (Solar, Bayan, Neon, Ube, Sampaguita, Kalikasan) and dark, light or system mode. Language & Region — English or Filipino menus, and your time zone.

On a computer On a phone Left edge: your Tambayans. Next column: channels or your DMs. Middle: the conversation. Right: members Bottom tabs: Home, Messages, Explore, Profile. Swipe from the left edge to open channels Ctrl + K (Windows) or ⌘ K (Mac) jumps to any channel or conversation Tap a conversation to open it full screen Sample data. What's new: after an update, Home shows a short summary until you've seen it, and the full post is in Diskarte HQ's #announcements channel (marked Official). Slow or expensive internet? Settings → Storage & Data → Low-data mode loads smaller images, stops GIFs from autoplaying and lowers video quality.

Plain-language help for using Diskarte. No technical knowledge needed. Guide You'll learn to Getting started Create an account, install Diskarte on your phone or computer, set up your profile Tambayans Create a Tambayan, invite friends, set up channels and run your community Messages Send messages, photos and voice notes, reply, react, search, schedule messages Calls Join voice channels, call friends, share your screen Events and Moments Schedule events, RSVP, and share 24-hour Moments Shared workspace Keep notes, task boards, focus timers, links and a whiteboard with your group Notifications, privacy and safety Control alerts, choose who can add you, block people, protect your account, download or delete your data Words you'll see Tambayan — a community (like a server or group). You can be in up to 100. Channel — a room inside a Tambayan: text (#), voice (speaker icon) or forum. Diskarte HQ — the official Tambayan everyone is in, for announcements. DM — a direct message between you and friends. Moderator / Admin / Owner — people who help run a Tambayan. Something not working? Settings → Report a problem sends a note to the Diskarte team.

Click Add a server (the + on the left rail; on phones, from Home). Give it a name and short description. Pick a template — Gaming crew, Study group, Creator community, Friend group, or Organization / team. Every template comes with a general chat and a voice channel; some add channels for resources and discussions. Done — you're the owner. Change anything later in Server settings.

Right-click your Tambayan (long-press on phones) → Invite people, or Copy invite link. Choose how long the link works (30 minutes up to "never") and how many people can use it. Friends open the link, sign in and join. You can also send the invite straight to a friend's DMs. Want strangers to find you? Admins can list the Tambayan in Explore with a category (Gaming, Study, Creators, Friends, Music, Tech, Anime, Sports, Other). People who were banned can't rejoin with any link. Screen new members (admins). Server settings → Membership: add up to 5 joining questions and, if you like, turn on Moderators approve new members. People joining then see your rules and questions first. With approval on, moderators review requests in the same tab (a "people want to join" button appears in the channel list when someone's waiting) and approve or decline them. Sample data.

Right-click the channel list → Create channel: Text for chatting, Voice for calls, Forum for titled posts with their own threads. Group channels into categories and drag them to reorder. Edit a channel to add a topic, slow mode (how often each person may post), read-only (only moderators post), or verified accounts only. Admins can make a channel private and choose which people or roles can see it.

Every member has a rank: Rank Can Member Chat, react, join calls, make invites, RSVP Moderator Also pin and delete messages, time out, warn, kick and ban members, manage channels, see the audit log Admin Also change settings, ranks and private channels Owner Everything, including deleting or transferring the Tambayan Change someone's rank or give them a custom role (a coloured label) by right-clicking them in the member list. Roles can unlock private channels.

Open Server settings from the Tambayan's menu. Admins see every tab; moderators see the audit log, bans and invites. Sample data. Tab Use it to Overview Name, icon, description, Explore listing, rules, welcome message, levels, export settings Roles Create coloured roles Bantay-Bayan Turn on auto-moderation: spam, scam links, hate speech, explicit content, and your own blocked words Audit log See who did what (joins, kicks, bans, deleted messages, auto-mod blocks…) Bans See bans and lift them Invites See and revoke invite links Emoji Upload up to 50 custom emoji Soundboard Upload short MP3 clips for calls Webhooks Let other apps post into a channel Announcements Post a message automatically every day or every week Support Add GCash/Maya numbers and grant supporter badges Rules: if you write rules, members must accept them before they can post. Change the rules and everyone is asked again. Welcome messages: greet new members automatically. Use {user} for their name and {server} for the Tambayan's name, e.g. Mabuhay {user}! Welcome sa {server}. Levels: members earn points for chatting (at most once a minute, so spamming doesn't help). A leaderboard shows the most active members. You can reset for a new season.

Right-click a member for: Timeout (60 seconds to a week) — they can read but not talk. Warn — they see your note once. Kick or Ban (with a reason). In a voice channel: mute, deafen, disconnect or move them. You can only act on people with a lower rank than yours. Everything is written to the audit log.
Leave server from the Tambayan's menu. Owners must hand the Tambayan to someone else or delete it first. Delete (owner only) removes all channels and messages permanently.

Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter. Shift + Enter starts a new line. Sample data. Mention someone with @username. Moderators can use @everyone, @here or a role. Format text with Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ``` for code blocks, ||spoiler|| to hide something until clicked. Attach photos, videos, MP3s (up to 10 files, 10 MB each) with the paperclip. Voice message: tap Record a voice message (mic button) and record up to 5 minutes. Stickers and GIFs: open the sticker or GIF picker; picking one sends it right away. Polls: ask a question with 2–10 answers, open for an hour up to a week. Shortcuts: start a message with /shrug, /tableflip, /unflip, /me or /spoiler (press Tab to complete). Links show a preview card. To hide a preview, wrap the link in < and >. No signal? Keep typing and sending — messages wait in a queue (you'll see an 8-bit "offline" bar) and send automatically when you're back online. If one fails, tap Retry. Why didn't my message send? You see Why "Slow mode — you can send again in …" The channel limits how often people post "Accept this server's rules first" Open the rules card above the message box and accept "You're sending too fast" Wait a few seconds A lock instead of the message box You're timed out, or only moderators can post here The message vanished Auto-moderation blocked it (spam, scam link or blocked word)

Hover a message (long-press on phones) for actions: Reply (or swipe right on a phone). React with Pinoy reactions like petmalu, lodi, sana all, or the Tambayan's custom emoji. Start thread to move a side discussion into its own panel. Edit or Delete your own messages. Edited messages show "(edited)"; you and moderators can see the earlier versions. Pin (moderators) — see all pins from the pin icon in the channel header. Save Message to bookmark it for yourself. Forward to another channel or a DM. Mark Unread to come back later.

Each new post needs a title. Replies go inside the post. Pinned posts stay on top, then the most active ones. Tags: pick up to 5 of the forum's tags when you post, or open your post to change them. Tap a tag above the list to show only those posts. Solved: open your question and tap Mark solved once it's answered. Suggestion boards: some forums collect ideas. Tap the arrow to upvote (tap again to take it back), use Top to see the most wanted ideas, and watch for the status a moderator sets: Under consideration, Planned, In progress, Completed or Declined. Moderators: the ⚙ button sets the forum's kind and its tags.

Right-click (long-press on phones) any message → Remind me… → pick a time. Diskarte saves the message and pops up a reminder with an Open button when it's time. Reminders show while Diskarte is open; if it's closed, you'll see it next time you open the app. Find pending reminders under Notifications → Saved.

In a text channel, open Schedule message next to the send button, write the message and pick a time up to 30 days ahead (you can have 25 waiting). Open Scheduled messages to see, cancel or check failed ones. A scheduled message posts as you, following the channel's rules; if it can't (for example you were timed out), it stays in the list with the reason. Scheduling isn't available in DMs.

In a Tambayan: use the search box in the channel header. Add from:username or in:channel to narrow it down. Everywhere: the Search page searches every Tambayan and DM you can read, with filters for sender, dates and media type. Click a result to jump to that exact message.

Add friends first: Friends → Add Friend → their @username. Message a friend from their profile or the Messages tab. Start a group DM with up to 9 friends. Under your latest message you'll see Sent or Seen. Right-click a DM to mark it read, see the person's options, or leave a group.

A Hangout is a quick, temporary space for you and up to 9 friends — chat plus a call — that cleans itself up afterwards. On Home, tap Start a Hangout (or the ✦ next to a friend who's around). Pick what it's for, who's coming and how long (1, 3 or 8 hours). Leave Jump into voice on to join the call right away and ring everyone. Anyone in it can add an hour. The host can Keep it (it becomes a normal group chat), Make it a Tambayan (everyone gets an invite), or End it. When the time runs out, the hangout and its messages are deleted. Files can't be shared in a hangout until it's kept. Sample data.
A white dot means new messages; a red number means someone mentioned you. Right-click a Tambayan → Mark As Read, or use Mark all as read in your inbox.

Click a channel with the speaker icon. You'll see who's inside. Click Join. Allow microphone access the first time. You stay in the call while you look at other channels, other Tambayans or your DMs. Sample data. Hover a Tambayan's icon (or long-press it and choose Voice activity) to see who's talking before you join. Leave with Disconnect in the "Voice Connected" panel (bottom left) or the call strip on phones.
Open a DM or group DM and press the call button. Everyone else in the conversation sees a ringing pop-up for 45 seconds and can accept or decline.

Button What it does Mic Mute / unmute Headphones Deafen (you hear nothing and can't talk) Camera Turn your video on/off Screen Share your screen or a window/tab (with sound if your browser allows). Click a shared screen to watch it; use focus mode for full screen Mixer Change the volume of each person, mute someone just for you, or stop seeing their video Soundboard Play a short sound everyone hears Activities Watch YouTube together, play Tic-Tac-Toe or Pinoy Trivia The signal bars show your connection quality; tap them for details. Settings → Voice & Video lets you choose your microphone and speakers, test your mic, pick a noise setting (Isolation for noisy places, Studio for good mics) and turn on push to talk (hold a key to speak).

Turn on Low-data mode (Settings → Storage & Data): video uses less data. Turn your camera off; audio uses very little data. If the page reloads during a call, Diskarte reconnects you automatically. No sound after reconnecting? Click the turn on sound button.
Right-click someone in a voice channel to mute, deafen, disconnect or move them to another channel.

See events: the Events row in a Tambayan's channel list shows how many are coming up (or LIVE when one has started). RSVP: open an event and press Interested. If the event has a limit and it's full, you'll see that. With notifications on, Diskarte reminds you 15 minutes before it starts. Add to your calendar: the Calendar button downloads a file your phone or computer calendar can import. Create an event (moderators): Open Events → schedule a new event. Give it a name, description, start and end time, and either a voice channel or another location. Optional: set a capacity (how many people can say they're coming). Optional: Repeat weekly for 4, 8 or 12 weeks — Diskarte creates each week as its own event, so you can change or cancel one without affecting the others. Events in a private channel are only visible to people who can see that channel.

Moments are short updates — text, a photo, or both — that disappear after 24 hours. Find them on Home. Share a moment: choose who sees it: all your friends or only your favourites. You can have up to 10 live moments. Mute someone to stop seeing their moments without unfriending them. Report a moment that breaks the rules; the Diskarte team reviews it. Delete your own moment anytime from its options. Mark friends as favourites from your Friends list.

Every Tambayan has a workspace for planning and studying together. Open it from the Tambayan's menu or channel list. Everything belongs to a text channel, and anyone who can see that channel can see its documents. Sample data. Tool Good for Note Meeting notes, reviewers, guides (Markdown) Task board To do / Doing / Done cards for a project or event Focus timer A shared study or work session (1–120 minutes) everyone counts down together Resources A list of useful links (https only) with descriptions Whiteboard Quick sketches and diagrams Editing together: when two people change the same document, Diskarte doesn't silently overwrite anyone. If someone saved while you were editing, you'll see their version and choose whether to keep yours or theirs. Your unsaved text stays until you decide. Can't edit? You might be timed out, the channel might be read-only, or it might require a verified email. On phones, editors open full screen; leaving with unsaved changes asks first.

Open Settings → Notifications: Sample data. Desktop notifications for new DMs while Diskarte is open in a tab. Sounds — the little 8-bit beeps. Change the volume from the speaker button next to your name. Quiet hours — no sounds, rings or alerts between times you choose. Pause for 1 hour — a quick break. This device (push notifications) — get alerts even when Diskarte is closed. Choose which kinds: DMs, mentions, replies, friend requests, invitations, calls, events, moderation and security. Previews are off by default, so your lock screen just says "Diskarte"; turn them on to see who wrote and what. On iPhone, install Diskarte to your home screen first (see Getting started). Push notifications also depend on your phone's focus modes and battery settings. Per Tambayan: Only @mentions, Nothing, or Mute Server (until you unmute, or Mute for 1 hour / Mute for 8 hours). This lives in the Tambayan's menu under Notification Settings. Right-click a channel → Mute Channel.

Who can add you: Settings → Privacy & Safety → everyone, only people in a Tambayan with you, or nobody. Sample data. DMs only come from friends. Friend nicknames and notes you add are visible only to you. Favourites are private too. Show friends when I'm around (Settings → Privacy & Safety): turn it off and friends won't see you as online or which voice channel you're in on their Home. Invisible always hides you. Seen receipts in DMs can't be turned off yet.
Right-click someone → Block. They can't message you or send you friend requests, and to them it looks like your account doesn't exist. Unblock from the same menu.

Use a strong, unique password. Turn on two-factor sign-in: Settings → My Account → Two-factor, then scan the code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password…). After that you'll enter a 6-digit code when you sign in. Keep your authenticator safe — losing it means asking an administrator for help. Settings → Devices & Sessions → sign out everywhere if you used a shared computer.

Download everything: Settings → Storage & Data → Request all of my data gives you a file with everything your account wrote or set. Delete your account: Settings → My Account → Danger zone. Type your username to confirm. Your files and private data are deleted. If you own Tambayans, they pass to their most senior member (or are deleted if nobody else is in them). This can't be undone.
Settings → Report a problem: choose what kind of problem, describe what happened, and send. The Diskarte team reviews every report.

Reply: hover/long-press → Reply, or swipe right on phones. A reply to a message in another channel is silently dropped to a plain message. Thread: start one from any top-level message; it opens in a side panel (full screen on phones, ThreadPanel). The root shows "N replies"; counters are trigger-maintained. Threads can't be nested (INVALID_THREAD).

Every top-level message is a post with a 1–100 character title (POST_TITLE_REQUIRED otherwise); replies go in the post's thread. Pinned posts come first, then latest activity (ForumView). Slow mode, auto-mod, timeouts and unreads apply. Feature Who Detail Forum kind and tags Moderators (forum ⚙) Discussion or Suggestion board; up to 12 tags, 20 characters, case-insensitively unique (set_forum_settings). Removing a tag takes it off every post Tagging a post Its author or a moderator Up to 5 of the forum's tags, when posting or from the open post (set_forum_post) Solved Its author or a moderator Discussion forums only Votes and statuses Members vote; moderators set statuses Suggestion boards only (toggle_forum_vote); see suggestion boards Filters Everyone Search, tag chips, status filter and Top sorting State lives in forum_post_state and forum_votes (readable by whoever can view the channel, written only through the functions, deleted with the post); forum_overview(channel) returns tags, status and vote totals. Migration 20261108020000_forum_tags_suggestions.sql. Tests: tests/db/forum.test.ts, tests/db/forum-suggestions.test.ts, tests/ui/forum.test.tsx.

Reactions are glyph codes, not emoji: the Pinoy set (:petmalu:, :lodi:, :sana_all:, :charot:, :canton:…), classic reactions, and the server's custom emoji. Up to 20 distinct reactions per message (TOO_MANY_REACTIONS). The right-click menu has a quick row (:thumbs_up:, :heart:, :laugh:, :petmalu:). Settings → Chat can hide reactions. lib/emoji.ts, ReactionBar.

Up to 10 files per message, 10 MB each: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP3, MP4, WebM/Ogg/MP4 audio. Files are checked by magic bytes in the browser, then by the action, the database trigger and the Storage policy. They live in the private attachments bucket at <server>/<channel>/<uploader>/<uuid>.<ext> and are shown through short-lived signed URLs (useSignedUrls). Images open in the media viewer with a gallery of the conversation's media (MediaViewer). Low-data mode serves smaller images, doesn't autoplay GIFs and doesn't preload videos. Deleting a message also deletes its files (uploader or a moderator).

Record up to 5 minutes from the composer (VoiceRecorder); the browser picks WebM/Opus, Ogg/Opus or MP4/AAC (Safari) at 32 kbps. They're uploaded as ordinary attachments. Test: src/components/chat/__tests__/voice-recorder.test.tsx, tests/db/voice-messages.test.ts.

The composer's poll button creates a message whose text is the question, with 2–10 answers, single or multiple choice, open for 1 h, 4 h, 8 h, 24 h, 3 days or a week (create_poll, vote_poll). Results update live over db:chat:<channel>:poll-<message>. Tests: tests/db/polls.test.ts, tests/ui/polls.test.tsx.

Stickers: two built-in packs (Salitang Kanto, Tambayan Classics) drawn as SVG; the database stores only the sticker id. GIFs: GIPHY search via /api/gifs (needs GIPHY_API_KEY, PG-13). A message that is only a GIPHY link renders as the GIF. Link previews: the first 3 distinct links outside code get a card via /api/unfurl (SSRF-guarded). Wrapping a link in <angle brackets> suppresses its preview; Settings → Chat can turn previews off. Test: src/components/chat/__tests__/link-embeds.test.tsx, tests/security/unfurl-routes.test.ts.

12 built-in synthesized 8-bit clips plus up to 24 uploaded MP3s per server (≤ 1 MB, checked for MP3 magic bytes, played for at most 6 s). Played to everyone in the call over the LiveKit data channel; one clip per person every 2 s; anyone can mute the soundboard for themselves.

A forum channel can be switched to a suggestion board (forum ⚙ → Forum settings, moderators): members post ideas and upvote them (one vote each; 30 votes a minute), and moderators set a status — Under consideration, Planned, In progress, Completed or Declined. Filter by status or tag and sort by Top. See Forum channels for tags and Solved posts.

No outgoing webhooks, bot users, slash-command apps or a general automation builder. Custom roles carry no permissions other than private-channel access. No server folders, vanity URLs or member screening questions. Badges and boosts are cosmetic; payments happen outside Diskarte.
Two levels: Bantay-Bayan tools inside each Tambayan (for its moderators and admins), and the Super Admin Control Center for the whole platform.

Category Catches Spam & flooding Repeated messages (the same text 3 times in a minute), mass mentions, "free nitro" and get-rich-quick scams Phishing links Fake GCash/Maya/bank/Discord/Steam links, IP loggers, lookalike (punycode) domains Hate speech Slurs targeting race, gender and disability Explicit content Porn sites and sexual terms (English and Tagalog) Custom words Admin's list, matched after leetspeak normalisation Moderators are exempt. Documents are not co-edited keystroke by keystroke. Each save sends the revision it was based on; save_workspace_document / save_workspace_asset only succeed if that is still the latest revision and then increment it. On a conflict: The editor keeps your local changes (nothing is overwritten). It shows the latest saved version. You explicitly choose to keep yours against the new revision (then save again) or take theirs. Other members' saves arrive live over Realtime. Leaving an editor with unsaved changes asks for confirmation. Losing access while editing shows a permission state instead of failing silently.

h: Do I need to download an app?
t: No. Diskarte works in your browser. You can also install it to your home screen like an app — see Create an account and install.

Only your friends can start a DM with you. You choose who can send you friend requests in Settings → Privacy & Safety: everyone, only people who share a Tambayan with you, or nobody. Block someone to stop them contacting you completely.

Messages in a Tambayan channel: members of that Tambayan (and, for a private channel, only the people and roles allowed in it). DMs: only the people in that conversation. Moments: your friends, or only your favourites if you choose. Messages are protected in transit and by access rules on the server. They are not end-to-end encrypted.

h: How many Tambayans can I join?
t: Up to 100.

h: Can I edit or delete a message?
t: Yes, your own. Hover (or long-press) the message and choose Edit or Delete. Edited messages show "(edited)"; you and the Tambayan's moderators can see earlier versions.

h: Why did my message disappear right after I sent it?
t: The Tambayan's auto-moderation probably blocked it (spam, a suspicious link or a blocked word). Ask a moderator if you think it was a mistake.

h: Does Diskarte work on slow or prepaid connections?
t: Yes. Turn on Low-data mode in Settings → Storage & Data. Messages you send while offline wait in a queue and go out when you reconnect. See Connection problems.

h: Can I use Diskarte in Filipino?
t: The main menus and settings can be shown in Filipino: Settings → Language & Region. Most other text is in English for now.

h: How do I get my data or delete my account?
t: Settings → Storage & Data → Request all of my data downloads everything your account wrote or set. Settings → My Account → Danger zone deletes your account permanently. See Notifications, privacy and safety.

What Diskarte stores, who can see it, and how to get it or delete it — in plain language. This page describes how the software and the official instance work today; it is not a legal agreement. Diskarte is open source, so anyone can run their own server: a self-hosted Diskarte is run by its own operators, who decide their own policies.

No ads, and no selling or sharing your data for advertising. No AI features: your messages aren't analysed, summarised or used to train anything. Voice and video calls aren't recorded. Audio and video travel through a media server (LiveKit) to the other people in the call; they are encrypted on the way, but not end-to-end. Messages are protected by access rules on the server and encrypted in transit; they are not end-to-end encrypted, so the service operators could technically access them.

When you post a link, our server fetches the page to build the preview, so the linked site sees our server, not you.

Tambayan moderators and admins can see their Tambayan's audit log, which includes short excerpts of messages they delete, and moderation actions. Platform administrators (the Diskarte team) can see account emails, sessions and devices, and can ban accounts or revoke sessions. Their actions are logged.

Messages, profiles and community data stay until you or a moderator delete them, or you delete your account. Moments disappear for viewers after 24 hours and are removed from the database a day later. A removed Moment's photo currently stays in storage until you delete your account. Notification delivery records are kept for 7 days.

The "backend" is split three ways, each with a clear job: Postgres is the source of truth for authorization. Every table has Row Level Security; field rules that RLS can't express (who may change a role, pin, edit) are BEFORE triggers; multi-row operations are SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that re-check the caller. The app never uses the service role for user-facing reads or writes, so a bug in a Server Action cannot widen access. Server Actions (src/actions/) are thin: validate with Zod, apply an in-process rate limit, call Supabase as the user, and translate database error codes (SLOWMODE, AUTOMOD_BLOCKED, RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED…) into readable messages. Many reads and simple writes skip actions entirely and go from the browser straight to PostgREST, where the same RLS applies. Route Handlers (src/app/api/) exist only where a server secret or a non-browser caller is involved: LiveKit tokens and webhooks, the push dispatcher and subscriptions, incoming channel webhooks, link previews (SSRF-guarded fetches), GIF search, voice previews, the admin snapshot and health. See the API reference. Only three server paths use the service-role key: the LiveKit webhook (to broadcast an invalidation), the push dispatcher (to claim jobs from the private outbox) and the one-off npm run admin:grant script.

The reasoning behind the larger choices is recorded in Architecture decision records. Free-tier first — single-instance in-memory rate limits (Upstash optional), lazy-loaded heavy SDKs, a 150 MB Docker image budget.

subscribeDbChanges(supabase, topic, bind, onStatus) wraps two non-obvious requirements: Authenticate the socket before joining. It awaits supabase.realtime.setAuth() first. realtime-js copies the access token into the join payload at subscribe() time; a join without it is evaluated as anon, and RLS filters out every row. Never reuse a dying channel. realtime-js returns the existing channel object for a topic until its removal round-trip completes. Re-subscribing in that window (switching away from a chat and straight back, React Strict Mode's double effects) would reuse a channel that never rejoins. removeChannelSafely() records each teardown and whenTopicFree() makes the next subscriber wait for it. Join status changes are recorded as session-only diagnostics (lib/diagnostics.ts), visible in Settings → Advanced → Connection diagnostics. They never include message text, ids, tokens or URLs.

Send — the client generates the message id (crypto.randomUUID()) and renders the row immediately with pending: true. The server's row (with server timestamps and author join) replaces it when the action returns. Rows are sorted by (created_at, id). Edit / delete / pin / react — applied locally first, rolled back if the action fails. Edits roll back only if the content hasn't changed again in the meantime. Reactions carry a per-message epoch so a slow snapshot refresh never overwrites a reaction the user just toggled; a message being reacted to is skipped by refreshes until its request settles.

The message id is the idempotency key. A retried insert whose first attempt already committed fails with 23505 (unique violation); sendMessageAction then selects the existing row (same id, channel and author) and reports success. No dedupe table or request id header is needed. Realtime INSERT events for an id already in the list replace that row instead of appending, and createOnce() (bounded, 500 ids) stops replays from playing a sound twice.

lib/outbox.ts persists unsent messages in localStorage: Entries are scoped to the signed-in account (userId) and target (channel/thread or DM); sign-out clears this device's queue. At most 50 entries; beyond that enqueue() refuses and the row shows as failed instead. Only text, reply/thread ids, sticker, title and the paths of already uploaded attachments are stored — never files or signed URLs. Flushing is sequential and stops at the first entry that is still offline, preserving order. useOutboxRetry retries every 2 s → 30 s (exponential) while the chat is open and visible, and immediately on online / visibilitychange, because the online event misses short outages. The 8-bit OfflineBanner shows while offline or while queued messages wait.

Realtime does not replay events missed while disconnected. useConversationRecovery closes the gap whenever the channel re-joins (SUBSCRIBED after the first join) or the browser fires online: sequenceDiagram participant H as useConversationRecovery participant DB as PostgREST (RLS) H->>H: snapshot = confirmed rows in view (no pending/queued/failed) loop known ids, 100 per request H->>DB: select … where id in (…) — picks up edits, pins, deletions end loop forward keyset pages of 100 H->>DB: select … where (created_at, id) > cursor order by created_at, id end H->>DB: get_reactions_snapshot(channel, ids) (channels only) H->>H: reconcileHistory(previous, snapshot, fetched, deletedIds) reconcileHistory() only replaces rows that are unchanged since the fetch began; anything edited, deleted or sent live during recovery wins. Deleted ids seen over Realtime are remembered (bounded to 1,000) so recovery can't resurrect them. Results are discarded if the user has switched conversation (scope check) before they arrive. Failures set recovery.problem, which the chat header surfaces with a Retry sync control. get_reactions_snapshot() reads reactions in one statement, avoiding offset-pagination races and PostgREST's row cap (20261014040000_reaction_snapshot.sql).

Channels. channels.last_message_at is maintained by a trigger; channel_reads stores when each user last read each channel; message_mentions stores who a message mentions (only people who can see the channel). UnreadsProvider loads my_unreads() and refreshes it every 30 s in the background (the open server is live via Realtime) and when the tab becomes visible. Durable receipts. Marking something read goes through lib/read-receipts.ts: queueRead(kind, id, at) stores "read up to at" in localStorage (diskarte:pending-reads), keeping the later of two marks. flushReads() sends mark_channel_read_until(p_channel, p_at) or mark_dm_read_until(p_conversation_id, p_at), one flush at a time. Confirmed receipts leave the queue; failures stay for the next try. Because a receipt names a moment, sending it late never marks newer messages read. The server caps p_at at its own clock. The moment is the later of this device's clock and the newest message's server timestamp, so a phone whose clock runs behind can't save a receipt older than what it showed (which used to bring read conversations back as unread after a reload). Unread is then an exact comparison of two database timestamps (lastMessageAt > lastReadAt); an earlier 500 ms tolerance hid a first message sent right after a conversation was opened. Mark Unread calls forgetRead() first, so a receipt that hasn't left the device cannot undo the user's intent, then mark_channel_unread. On databases older than 20261015010000_notification_read_

PresenceProvider keeps one ref-counted presence channel per server (server:<id>), shared by the open server view, the voice call (even while browsing another server) and voice previews. Each client tracks one payload: { user_id, status, custom_status, custom_status_emoji, voice_channel_id, muted, deafened, video, screen, online_at } flattenPresence() collapses multiple tabs to one entry per user (newest wins). Speaking indicators are Broadcast events on the same channel, sent on start/stop plus a heartbeat while talking; a claim lapses after SPEAKING_TTL_MS (3.5 s) so a dropped tab can't leave someone "talking". Separately, SessionGuard sends heartbeat_device() so the Control Center can show per-device last activity (offline after two missed minutes).

useTyping broadcasts typing at most every 2.5 s while the user types and stop on send/blur, on the private channel:<id> topic. Receivers expire an entry after 6 s without a refresh. Nothing is stored.

DM calls and "ring to voice" pings use the call_rings table (20261004000000_call_rings.sql). Clients never write it directly: ring_call(kind, target, callee?, video?) validates the relationship (DM participants, or fellow server members for a voice channel; never across a block), dedupes already-ringing callees and rate-limits. Each ring lives 45 seconds. respond_ring(ring, accept) lets the callee accept or decline; cancel_rings(target) lets the caller hang up first. Answering a ring older than 45 s marks it missed and refuses it; an unanswered ring otherwise simply stays ringing and clients ignore it once expired. Callees receive rings over db:rings:<me>; IncomingCalls shows the pop-up. Accepting joins the room through the normal token flow. Mute removes MICROPHONE from the participant's allowed sources and mutes the live track; deafen sets canSubscribe: false.

Server-assigned fields. Insert triggers overwrite author_id with auth.uid(), created_at with now(), and clear pin/edit fields, so clients can't backdate or impersonate. Immutable relationships. Guards refuse moving members, messages, events or channels between servers after creation (MEMBER_IMMUTABLE_FIELD and similar). Attachments must be objects in the attachments bucket under <server>/<channel>/<uploader>/<uuid>.<ext>, of an allow-listed MIME type and ≤ 10 MB — checked by the message trigger, the bucket configuration and the upload policy. This guide explains how identity, sessions and authorization work end to end. The threat model, the full control-by-control table and how to report a vulnerability are in the repository's SECURITY.md; this page links to it rather than repeating it.
Diskarte uses Supabase Auth (email + password, optional GitHub / Google / Discord OAuth, TOTP two-factor). All auth forms are Server Actions in app/(auth)/actions.ts.

Accounts carrying user_metadata.must_change_password (created with a temporary password) are sent to /reset-password?first=1 from the proxy, the login action and every protected render.

Settings → Account → Two-factor (TwoFactorSettings) enrols an authenticator app with supabase.auth.mfa.enroll, verifies the first code and can unenrol after re-verifying. The Auth API itself (where the code is verified) is unaffected (20261013160000_mfa_enforcement.sql).

/forgot-password → requestPasswordResetAction (always answers "If an account exists…") → Supabase emails a link to /auth/callback?next=/reset-password → recovery session → /reset-password → changePasswordAction.

Pulse is the redesign (Direction A, "Canvas": Spaces navigator, Conversation Canvas, Context sheet) in warm ink (dark) or paper (light) with a solar gold signature. It is built alongside Classic and reached per browser through the shell preference (ADR 016). This section covers the groundwork: tokens, fonts and the lint guard. No Pulse screen exists yet.

The diskarte-shell cookie (classic default, pulse) is read by the root layout, which renders <html data-shell="classic|pulse"> on the first byte (lib/shell.ts). Every token lives in pulse.css under html[data-shell="pulse"], so Classic computes exactly the same styles as before. The Tailwind aliases (bg-pulse-surface…) are @theme inline, so they only resolve inside Pulse. setShell(shell, router) flips the attribute, saves the cookie and calls router.refresh(); no reload, so a live call, open chats and drafts survive the switch. There is no visible toggle yet.

Short records of decisions that shape the codebase. Each was reconstructed from the code, migration comments and release notes; the date is when the decision shows up in history. New decisions use the ADR template and are appended here. # Decision Status 001 Authorization lives in Postgres (RLS, triggers, definer RPCs) Accepted 002 Runtime configuration; one image for every environment Accepted 003 Private Realtime channels only Accepted 004 Client-generated message ids for idempotent sends Accepted 005 The LiveKit call lives in the persistent app layout Accepted 006 Self-contained app folder, not an npm workspace Accepted 007 Hosted-only jobs are installed outside migrations Accepted 008 Database outbox for Web Push Accepted 009 Additive, forward-only migrations applied by hand Accepted 010 Free-tier first Accepted 011 Vercel for production, Docker kept portable Accepted 012 Vector glyph vocabulary instead of emoji Accepted 013 Help Center rendered at authoring time inside the app Accepted 014 Release announcements published by the deployment itself Accepted 015 Hangouts are temporary group conversations Accepted 016 Pulse ships behind a per-browser shell preference Accepted

Context. The browser talks to Supabase directly (PostgREST, Realtime, Storage) for most reads and many writes; Server Actions are only one of several paths. Decision. Every table has RLS; field-level rules (who may change a role, pin, edit, move a channel between servers) are BEFORE triggers raising coded exceptions (ONLY_MODERATORS_CAN_PIN, SLOWMODE…); multi-step operations are SECURITY DEFINER functions with search_path = '' that re-check auth.uid(). anon has no table privileges. The app never uses the service role for user requests. Consequences. One rule set covers every path. UI permission helpers (e.g. canManageMember in lib/servers.ts) only mirror database rules to hide controls. New functions must explicitly revoke … from public, anon because Supabase's default privileges grant EXECUTE to authenticated and anon.

Decision. lib/env.ts reads process.env per request and validates it with Zod; the root layout passes public values to the client through RuntimeConfigProvider instead of NEXT_PUBLIC_* build-time inlining. Consequences. The same Docker image runs locally, in CI and in production. Missing configuration shows a ConfigNotice instead of crashing, and /api/health reports it.

Context. On 2026-10-02 production had Realtime's "Allow public access" off and public Postgres Changes subscriptions silently delivered nothing. Decision. All channels are private; can_access_realtime_topic() authorizes every topic prefix; subscribeDbChanges() sets the socket's JWT before joining. Consequences. New topics need a migration. CI can't catch a public subscription (local Supabase allows them), so reviews must.

Decision. The composer generates the message UUID; retries reuse it; the server treats a unique violation as "already sent". Consequences. Idempotent offline queues without a dedupe table; Realtime echoes reconcile by id.

h: 005. The call lives in the root app layout
t: Decision. CallProvider is mounted by app/(app)/layout.tsx; settings open as a dialog. Consequences. Calls survive navigation. A full reload (including after a deploy) still drops the call, mitigated by the 30-second sessionStorage rejoin.

Context. Render (and Vercel) build with Root Directory diskarte and can't see files above it. Decision. The app has its own lockfile and Dockerfile; the root package.json only forwards scripts. The retired early-access portal was deleted rather than shared. Consequences. Nothing needed at build time may live outside diskarte/. Documentation and migrations may.

Decision. pg_cron, pg_net and Vault setup live in diskarte/docs/sql/*.sql, run once by the database owner. Consequences. Migrations run unmodified in PGlite and CI. Features degrade gracefully when the jobs aren't installed (see background-jobs.md).

Decision. Triggers enqueue push work in the same transaction as the source row; an authenticated HTTP dispatcher drains it with leases. Consequences. No message is pushed for a rolled-back insert; access is rechecked at send time; delivery is at least once. Requires pg_net, Vault and a reachable dispatcher URL.

Decision. Migrations add tables/columns/functions and replace functions; they don't drop user data. They are reviewed and applied by hand (SQL Editor or supabase db push), never by a deploy. Consequences. App rollbacks never require schema rollbacks — older code ignores new columns. New features must tolerate a database that hasn't been migrated yet (hide the feature, show a "couldn't" toast or an unavailable state).

Decision. Defaults fit Supabase/LiveKit/Render free tiers: in-memory rate limits (Upstash optional), lazy heavy SDKs, NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=384, a 150 MB image budget enforced in CI. Consequences. On multi-instance hosts (Vercel), set Upstash for shared auth rate limits; the link preview cache is per instance.

Context. 2026-10-12: Render's free tier sleeps and cold-starts slowly. Decision. Production runs on Vercel (diskarte-ten.vercel.app, functions next to the Supabase region). The Docker image and render.yaml stay supported; the proxy 308-redirects page requests on any host other than SITE_URL. Consequences. Vercel deploys main on push, in parallel with CI — watch CI and load a page after every push. Serverless instances don't share memory.

Decision. Reactions, statuses, badges and activities are :code: strings rendered as vector icons by <Glyph> (lib/glyphs.ts); the database validates reaction codes. Consequences. Consistent rendering across platforms; custom server emoji use the same :name: syntax backed by images.

h: 013. Help Center rendered at authoring time inside the app
t: Status. Accepted — 2026-11-06 Context. The Markdown docs live in the repository root, but hosts build only diskarte/. A public Help Center needed search, navigation and diagrams without new infrastructure or a heavier signed-in app. Decision. scripts/build-docs-site.mts renders the pages listed in docs/site.json to HTML and a search index, committed inside the app (like the generated database reference) and served at /docs by the existing Next.js app. Pages are Server Components that inject the pre-rendered HTML; only search, copy buttons, the table-of-contents highlight and Mermaid (lazy, only on pages with diagrams) run in the browser. Alternatives considered. Fumadocs/Nextra (a second app or MDX pipeline, a separate deploy and a styling system to reconcile); rendering Markdown per request (ships a parser and highlighter to the server for every view); an external search service (cost, and private pages could leak into it). Consequences. No new deployment; the docs inherit the app's themes, CSP and fonts. Authors run npm run docs:site after editing published Markdown (the docs test fails otherwise). Publication is an explicit allow-list, so new runbooks stay off the site by default.

h: 014. Release announcements published by the deployment itself
t: Status. Accepted — 2026-11-07 Context. Each meaningful release should be announced in Diskarte HQ, but only once it is actually live: not on push, not for failed or preview builds. There is no GitHub CLI or repository secret available to wire a CI step, and pushes to main deploy on Vercel in parallel with CI. Decision. A production server instance announces its own release from instrumentation.ts register() (opt-in RELEASE_ANNOUNCEMENTS=on, production only). Notes are developer-written JSON formatted deterministically. A service-role-only SQL function posts once per release under an advisory lock and refuses older releases after newer ones. Alternatives considered. A GitHub Actions job on Vercel's deployment_status (needs a repository secret and an exposed publish endpoint); a Vercel deployment webhook (plan-dependent, another secret); publishing from CI on merge (would announce failed deployments). Consequences. Every instance start costs one cheap RPC (not awaited). If the first attempt fails, the next instance retries. Super admins can retry, withdraw or republish in the Control Center.

Status. Accepted — 2026-11-08 Context. Friends needed a spontaneous way to talk and call without creating a permanent Tambayan, and without leaving abandoned rooms or files behind. Decision. A Hangout is a dm_conversations group row with an end time (hangout_until). It reuses group-DM text, read state, Realtime, the DM call room and rings unchanged. Expired hangouts stop accepting messages immediately (trigger) and are deleted by purge_expired_hangouts (platform job, and whenever a hangout is created). Uploads are refused while temporary so deletion never orphans Storage objects; "Keep" clears the end time. Alternatives considered. A new hangouts table with its own messages and LiveKit rooms (duplicates DMs, calls and their RLS); temporary Tambayans (channels, roles and invites are far more than a quick get-together needs, and cleanup would touch many tables). Consequences. Every DM code path already handles hangouts; the UI only adds the end-time bar, list badges and the start dialog. Hangouts follow group-DM rules (friends only, ≤ 10 people). Files need the hangout to be kept first.

h: 016. Pulse ships behind a per-browser shell preference
t: Status. Accepted — 2026-11-08 Context. The Diskarte Pulse redesign (Spaces navigator, Conversation Canvas, Context sheet) replaces the whole look. It has to be built and tested in production-like conditions over several releases while Classic, the current UI, stays exactly as it is for everyone else. Decision. A diskarte-shell cookie (classic by default, or pulse) is read by the root layout, which server-renders <html data-shell> like the theme and colour mode. Every Pulse style is scoped to html[data-shell="pulse"] (pulse.css) and Pulse components live in components/pulse/, lint-restricted to Pulse tokens. Switching sets the attribute, writes the cookie and calls router.refresh() (lib/shell.ts), never a full reload, so the call and session providers in the (app) layout stay mounted. Alternatives considered. A separate route tree or app (duplicates data loading and would drop the call when switching); a server-side flag per account (needs a migration and makes a stuck user unable to switch back in another browser); a localStorage flag (the server can't see it, so the first paint would flash the wrong shell). Consequences. Classic needs no changes and its tests prove it is untouched. Pulse fonts load only when Pulse styles use them. Until there is a visible switch, Pulse is reached by setting the cookie. The preference is per browser, like the theme; syncing it across devices would be a later decision.

TypeScript strict is on. Prefer inferred types; use z.infer for anything validated. Validate every trust boundary with Zod (lib/schemas/*): action inputs, route bodies, query params, JSON from storage. Never trust a client-provided user id — the server uses the session. Import with the @/ alias (@/lib/…, @/components/…). Server-only modules import server-only; secrets are read only in those modules. A test fails if a "use client" module references a server secret. lib/supabase/database.types.ts mirrors the schema; update it with new tables/columns/functions. Read runtime config through useSupabase() / RuntimeConfigProvider, never NEXT_PUBLIC_*. Heavy UI (LiveKit, pickers, settings bodies, admin) loads lazily with a skeleton. Realtime: use subscribeDbChanges() for Postgres Changes and always private: true channels. Optimistic updates must roll back on failure and show a specific toast. Follow the lint rules from eslint-config-next (core web vitals + TypeScript), including the React Compiler rules; justify any eslint-disable inline. The schema is the security boundary, so migrations get the most careful review in this repository.

One file per change in supabase/migrations/, named YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_short_name.sql with a timestamp later than every existing file. Never edit a migration that has been applied anywhere shared; write a new one. Additive and forward-only. Add tables, columns, indexes and functions; replace functions with create or replace. Don't drop user data. Older app versions must keep working against the new schema, and new app code must tolerate the migration not being applied yet (hide the feature or show an "unavailable" state). Start with a comment block explaining what the migration adds and why. Put a -- comment directly above every create table and create function; the generated database reference uses it as the description. Portable SQL only. Migrations must run unmodified in PGlite (tests) and the CI Supabase stack. Anything needing pg_cron, pg_net or Vault goes in diskarte/docs/sql/*.sql as a reviewed, re-runnable installer. Applied by hand. Deploys never run migrations. Document every new file in the changelog / release notes with its order and what breaks without it.

For each new or changed table, policy, trigger or definer function, the reviewer answers: Can a signed-out visitor (anon) read or call it? It should be "no" unless it's a deliberate public endpoint (like get_invite, username_available, post_webhook_message). Can a signed-in non-member see or change it? Can a member act on someone else's rows, or impersonate them? Can a moderator act on an equal or higher rank? Can anyone change their own rank? Does a private channel stay private through every path: table, search, Realtime topic, push, events, workspace? Does a banned, timed-out or MFA-pending session get refused where it should? Does a definer function leak existence (different errors for "not found" vs "forbidden") where that matters? What happens on account deletion and in the data export? Each "no" needs a PGlite test that proves it (see testing.md → Database / RLS tests).

Diskarte exposes three kinds of interface: HTTP route handlers under /api/* and /auth/* — documented below with real request/response shapes. Server Actions ("use server" functions in diskarte/src/actions/) — called by React components, not a public API. Supabase PostgREST / RPC — the browser and server query tables and call functions as the signed-in user; RLS decides what they see. The full function list with signatures and who may call each one is in the database reference. There is no public, versioned REST API for third parties. The only endpoint meant for outside callers is the incoming channel webhook.

Base URL: SITE_URL (production: https://diskarte-ten.vercel.app). Authentication: Supabase session cookies (sb-*), set by sign-in. Route handlers call supabase.auth.getUser(); there are no API keys or bearer tokens for users. CSRF: proxy.ts rejects non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests to /api/* whose Origin (or Referer) isn't the site's own origin or listed in ALLOWED_ORIGINS → 403 {"error":"Cross-site request blocked"}. Exempt: /api/livekit/webhook, /api/push/dispatch and /api/webhooks/<id>/<token> (they authenticate with their own secret). CORS: only the site origin and ALLOWED_ORIGINS receive Access-Control-Allow-* headers (credentials allowed, GET, POST, OPTIONS, max-age 600 s). Called by LiveKit Cloud. Body ≤ 64 KB; the Authorization header must be LiveKit's signed JWT (verified with LIVEKIT_API_KEY/SECRET, including the body hash). For participant_joined, participant_left, participant_connection_aborted, track_published, track_unpublished and room_finished on a voice:<uuid> room, it broadcasts an empty voice_changed event on the server's private server:<id> topic. Returns 204 (handled or ignored), 401 (bad signature), 413, or 503 (database/broadcast failure, so LiveKit retries). Needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.

?serverId=<uuid> → { channels: PreviewChannel[], limited: boolean } where each channel has id, name, count, participants[≤8] { id, profile, muted, screen }, streamers[]. The endpoint must be an allow-listed push vendor over HTTPS; the P-256 key is validated. Errors: 400 invalid, 401, 403 (MFA pending; not for remove), 413, 429 (PUSH_RATE_LIMIT from the database: wait a minute), 503 (push not configured).

Internal: called by the database (pg_net) with Authorization: Bearer <PUSH_DISPATCH_SECRET>. The body is ignored — recipients and payloads come only from the database. Returns the batch counts as JSON, 401 (wrong secret), 503 (secret missing/shorter than 32 characters, VAPID/service role missing, or queue failure). maxDuration = 60 s. See background-jobs.md.

The integration endpoint. An admin creates the URL in Server settings → Webhooks; the token is shown once (48 hex characters) and stored only as a hash. curl -X POST "https://diskarte-ten.vercel.app/api/webhooks/$WEBHOOK_ID/$WEBHOOK_TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"content":"Build #42 passed ✅","username":"CI"}' { "id": "a7d3…" } Field Rules content Required string, 1–2000 characters (Discord-compatible name, so existing scripts work) username Optional display name for this post (stored as webhook_name, ≤ 32 chars) Status Body 200 { "id": "<message uuid>" } 400 Send JSON: {"content": "…"} · content must be 1–2000 characters · username must be text 404 Unknown webhook (bad id/token format, wrong token, deleted webhook or channel) 413 Body over 16 KB 429 Slow down: 30 messages a minute, Retry-After: 60 503 Couldn't post Webhook posts have no author, can't ping @everyone/@here, and go through the database function post_webhook_message, which is executable by anon only and verifies the token hash. The proxy still rate-limits the path per IP (120/min).

?url=<http(s) URL ≤ 2048 chars> → { "preview": { url, siteName, title, description, image, color } | null }. Fetched server-side through lib/ssrf.ts: default ports only, every resolved address must be public (checked at connect time to defeat DNS rebinding), redirects re-checked by hand, 512 KB and 5 s caps. image is rewritten to a signed /api/unfurl/image URL. Results are cached per instance for 1 hour (500 entries). 400 Link not allowed, 401, 429.

?u=<image url>&s=<signature> — only URLs signed by /api/unfurl (HMAC-SHA256 with a key derived from LIVEKIT_API_SECRET). Returns PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP ≤ 3 MB with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox, nosniff and a 1-day immutable cache. 403 bad signature or blocked host, 404 not an allowed image, 502 upstream failure. This exists because the CSP blocks third-party images.

?q=<≤50 chars>&offset=<n> (trending when q is empty) → { gifs: [{ id, title, preview, width, height, url }], next: number | null }. Pages of 24, rated PG-13. 503 when GIPHY_API_KEY isn't set, 401, 429, 502.

Super admins only (proxy and handler both check is_super_admin(); every RPC checks again). ?q=<≤64 chars> filters the roster server-side. Returns { overview, users, voice, audit, broadcasts, reports, traffic, generatedAt } in one round trip. 401, 403, 500 (migration missing).

Super admins only (proxy, handler and every RPC check). Body { "action": "publish" | "withdraw" | "reset", "id": "<release id from src/content/releases.json>" }. Action Effect publish Posts the release now (service role, same path as the automatic post); { "result": "published" | "already-published" | "superseded" | "failed" } withdraw Deletes the post and keeps the record, so it isn't posted again automatically; { "result": "withdrawn" } reset Deletes the post and the record, then publishes the current notes again 400 unknown release, 403 not a super admin, 503 migration missing, service role key missing or publishing failed. See release announcements.

h: 2026-11-08 — Hangouts, membership screening, suggestion boards, reminders
t: Added Instant Hangouts: temporary group chats with a call for you and 1–9 friends, lasting 1–24 hours. Start one from Home, jump straight into voice and ring everyone; anyone adds an hour, the host keeps it, turns it into a Tambayan or ends it. Expired hangouts are deleted with their messages and take no file uploads. Added friends who are around on Home: online friends first, their status and the voice channel they're in when you can see it. Invisible friends and anyone who turns off Settings → Privacy → "Show friends when I'm around" never appear. Added membership screening: up to 5 joining questions and optional moderator approval, with a live queue in Server settings → Membership, a sidebar nudge for moderators and audit-log entries. Answers are included in the applicant's data export. Added forum tags, Solved posts and pinned-first sorting, and suggestion boards with one-per-member upvotes, Top sorting and moderator statuses (Under consideration, Planned, In progress, Completed, Declined). Added Remind me… on server messages: saved with a time and shown with a jump link (and a desktop notification when enabled) while Diskarte is open. Needs four migrations: 20261108000000_hangouts.sql, 20261108010000_membership_screening.sql, 20261108020000_forum_tags_suggestions.sql, 20261108030000_message_reminders.sql. Existing features keep working without them; until they're applied the new actions fail with an error message.

h: 2026-11-07 — smoother start, dependable notifications, release posts
t: Fixed unread state missing a message sent within half a second of opening a conversation or of reading it (also the cause of the intermittently failing notification E2E journey): unread is now an exact comparison of database timestamps. Fixed read DMs and channels coming back as unread on devices whose clock runs behind the server: receipts now cover the newest message shown. Added a Getting started checklist and a What's New card on Home, with Filipino strings; a first-time greeting replaces "Welcome back" for new members. Added official release announcements: each production deployment posts its developer-written release notes (src/content/releases.json) once to Diskarte HQ #announcements as "Diskarte Updates" with an Official badge; super admins can retry, withdraw or republish in the Control Center. Added a plain-language Privacy and your data page, linked from the landing page, sign-up form and Help Center. Needs migration 20261107000000_release_announcements.sql, then RELEASE_ANNOUNCEMENTS=on (Production only) with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, for the release posts. Everything else works without it.

Added the public Help Center at /docs: user guides, help and troubleshooting, the feature reference, developer docs, the API reference and this changelog, with search (Ctrl/⌘ K), section filters, breadcrumbs, an on-page contents list, previous/next links, copyable code, rendered diagrams, product screenshots, dark/light/system modes and a phone layout. Added contextual help links in Settings (every section), server settings, the voice lobby, the shared workspace, an empty Tambayan and the sign-in page, plus Help Center links on the landing page. h: 2026-10-15 — live voice activity and Web Push
t: Added authorized LiveKit hover previews and mobile long-press sheets, with shared Realtime updates and signed webhook invalidation. Added a private, transactional Web Push outbox, per-device session-bound subscriptions, leased dispatch, retries, event reminders, and invalid endpoint cleanup. Prevented delayed push registration/reconciliation from restoring an account binding after logout; failed reconnects preserve existing subscriptions. Added notification installation guidance, device management, synchronized delivery preferences, safe deep links, and private lock-screen defaults using the existing service worker. Added queue/RLS, transport encryption, permission, worker-only browser, and interaction regressions; restored dialog focus as soon as dismissal begins. Updated Next.js to 16.4.1, Sharp to 0.35.5 and source-map-js to 1.2.2; the production dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities. ESLint’s unpatched development dependency advisories remain documented. Push remains disabled until production secrets and the reviewed database setup are configured. See docs/web-push.md.

Added revisioned private draft/preference sync, private DM media, history anchors and reconnect reaction reconciliation. Added community templates/settings export, discovery pagination, shared resources and saved collaborative whiteboards. Added atomic event capacity, canonical RSVP summaries and finite weekly scheduling. Added light/system appearance, core Filipino navigation/settings translations and time-zone preferences. Improved keyboard viewport overlays and focus behavior; secured account export/deletion for newly persisted data. Removed the AI report action/workflow while retaining manual reports and history. Expanded migration readiness checks and multi-user browser regression coverage. See the follow-up delivery report for exact results, migrations and unfinished scope.

Distinguished missing workspace migrations from connection, session and permission failures; added a read-only database readiness command and CI gate. Added moderator event editing with concurrent-change detection, confirmed cancellation and timezone-safe calendar export; improved mobile form sizing, RSVP request deduplication and reconnect refresh. Prevented abandoned conversation recovery requests and deferred bottom-scroll callbacks from affecting a later view. Recovered missed event/RSVP deletion notifications with bounded, permission-checked refresh while Events is open; suspended polling for hidden, offline and closed views. Added mobile destination tabs, keyboard-aware viewport, persistent call strip, swipe-to-reply and virtualized DM history. Restored optional floating desktop panels and added a lazy keyboard navigation palette. Added public community discovery, permission-aware global message search and historical message context. Added channel-scoped shared notes, task boards and database-clock focus timers with concurrency checks. Added safe PWA static caching, offline fallback, install/update controls, persistent local drafts, upload retry/cleanup, quiet hours and accessibility surface controls. Fixed message retry identity, queue account isolation, concurrent rollback, cancelled call joins, muted rejoin behavior and reconnect history gaps. Restricted private-channel events and RSVP visibility; added structured server errors and session-only connection diagnostics
